chunk.text: Elliot Ramirez sat at the corner table of a quiet café, his laptop open and his fingers hovering over the keyboard. The screen displayed a group photo from his past, one that had once brought him joy but now only stirred a deep sense of nostalgia and regret. He had been trying for weeks to delete his Friendster account, a digital relic of a romantic relationship that had ended more than a year ago. Gary Thompson, his best friend, noticed Elliot’s hesitation and approached the table with concern. Gary sat down, asking, 'Hey, man. You okay? You looked like you were about to cry when you saw that photo.' Elliot sighed, 'I don’t know, Gary. I’ve been trying to delete my Friendster account for weeks, but every time I see a photo from that time, I freeze.' Mia Chen, seated at the next table, chimed in, 'Sometimes letting go of the past means you’re finally ready to grow, Elliot.' Elliot looked at them both, 'I know. I just... I feel like I’m losing a part of me if I delete it. But maybe I’m holding on to something that’s not helping me anymore.' Gary placed a hand on his shoulder and said, 'Whatever you decide, I’m here. Just remember, you’re not alone in this.' Elliot nodded, then opened the photo again and hesitated before closing it.
